correctness.rationale: Exact two-circle six-point DFT forces the k=0 polynomial to have roots at two distinct positive radii squared, the k=1 quadratic to factor into those roots, the k=2 linear coefficient to vanish, and the k=3 Nyquist phase to vanish exactly under nonzero sine. This yields all four real kernel parameters. For nonzero neighbor coefficient the Hermitian kernel is irreducible tridiagonal, so nullity at most one; for zero neighbor coefficient it is diagonal with at least three nonzero entries since a binomial cannot have two distinct positive roots. Thus every nonzero kernel matrix has rank at least three, excluding differences of rank-one signal matrices. Explicit inequivalent polynomial pairs settle both converse obstructions. The packaged checker gave VERIFY_OK 1430 comparisons.

value.rationale: Balanced two-ring samples are a natural practical measurement design in complex polynomial phase retrieval, while previous sharp-size constructions use asymmetric 7+5 or intersecting rings. The theorem classifies EVERY choice of positive radii and rotation angles and all cubic coefficient vectors, gives two explicit independent geometric obstructions, and exhibits the exact four-dimensional lifted nullspace with a nonstandard tridiagonal rank rigidity proof. This is a motivated structural classification, not a numerical recheck or unmotivated parameter slice.
